what_its_for: Zafirlukast helps prevent and control asthma symptoms in adults and children 5 years and older. It works by blocking certain natural substances in your body (called leukotrienes) that cause swelling and tightening in your airways, making it easier to breathe. It is used every day to help prevent asthma attacks, but it does NOT work fast enough to treat a sudden asthma attack.
how_to_take: Take zafirlukast by mouth, exactly as your doctor prescribed. Swallow the tablet whole with a full glass of water. Take it on an EMPTY STOMACH, at least 1 hour before or 2 hours after a meal, because food can reduce how well the medicine works. Take it at the same times each day (usually twice a day, morning and evening) to keep a steady level in your body. Do not stop taking it without talking to your doctor, even if you feel well.
dosing: Adults and teenagers (12 years and older): The usual dose is 20 mg twice a day. Children ages 5 to 11 years: The usual dose is 10 mg twice a day. Always follow your doctor's specific instructions, as your dose may be different based on your needs.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next scheduled dose, skip the missed dose and continue with your regular schedule. Do NOT take two doses at the same time to make up for a missed one.
storage: Store zafirlukast tablets at room temperature, between 68°F and 77°F (20°C and 25°C). Keep the tablets in their original container, away from light and moisture. Do not store in the bathroom. Keep all medications safely out of reach of children and pets. Do not use tablets past the expiration date printed on the packaging.
what_to_avoid: Avoid taking zafirlukast with food, as it reduces how well the medicine is absorbed. Avoid drinking large amounts of alcohol, as it may increase the risk of liver problems. Tell your doctor and pharmacist about ALL medicines you take, including over-the-counter drugs and supplements. Zafirlukast can interact with blood thinners like warfarin (Coumadin), aspirin, erythromycin, theophylline, and other medications, causing dangerous effects. Do NOT use this medicine to treat a sudden asthma attack — always have a fast-acting rescue inhaler (like albuterol) available for sudden symptoms.
when_to_call_doctor: Contact your doctor right away if you experience: yellowing of your skin or eyes, dark urine, severe stomach pain, unusual tiredness, or loss of appetite (these could be signs of liver problems); a worsening of asthma symptoms or more frequent use of your rescue inhaler; tingling or numbness in your arms or legs; flu-like symptoms with a skin rash; signs of an allergic reaction such as hives, swelling of the face, lips, tongue, or throat, or difficulty breathing; or feeling depressed, anxious, having trouble sleeping, or unusual changes in behavior or mood.
when_it_works: Zafirlukast starts working within a few days, but it may take 1 to 2 weeks of regular use before you notice the full benefit. It must be taken every day to work properly, even when you feel fine and have no symptoms. Do not stop taking it just because you feel better.
special_populations: Older adults (65 years and older): Older patients may be more sensitive to this medication and have a higher risk of infections. Your doctor may monitor you more closely. Pregnancy and breastfeeding: Talk to your doctor before taking zafirlukast if you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding. Liver problems: This medicine is NOT recommended if you have liver disease. Tell your doctor about any liver problems before starting this medication. Children under 5 years: Zafirlukast is not approved for use in children younger than 5 years old.
